# Module `chain`

chain - hash-chained legitimization core.

A hash-chained ledger of small, named records used to *legitimize* an
artifact: an OS package (VybForge), a boot/generation (VybOS), or a
smuggled-in dependency's identity (Vyb `smuggle`). One shared core, three
consumers — every consumer seals its facts into a `Chain` and gets back a
tamper-evident tip hash (the "legit token") it can later re-verify.

Model (the exact shape pre-flight-pinned by VybOS's
repro/probe_vyb_chain_primitives.vyb):
  Record       { label, value }          one fact to seal
  ChainBlock   { index, prev_hash, root, hash, records }
  Chain        { origin, blocks }

Each block:
  root       = the Merkle root over its records (pair-fold of per-record
               SHA-256 digests; odd nodes duplicate the last leaf).
  hash       = sha256(index | prev_hash | root)
  prev_hash  = the previous block's hash (block 0 uses the chain `origin`).

`verify` recomputes every root, hash and prev-link; any tamper with a
record, order, or link breaks it. This is content integrity, NOT a
signature: it binds the facts to the chain's `origin` marker but the
origin is a shared constant, so anyone can forge a chain that verifies.
Authenticity/authorship needs real signatures (#204 freedom capability) —
this core deliberately stops at integrity.

Usage:
  import chain::{new_chain, append, verify, tip_hash, contains, Record}
  r<Vec<Record>> = Vec()
  r.push(Record { label = "name", value = "busybox" })
  r.push(Record { label = "version", value = "1.36.1" })
  c<Chain> = new_chain("vybforge/forge-1", r)
  println(tip_hash(c))
  println(if (verify(c)) { "LEGIT" } else { "TAMPERED" })

NOTE: Vyb ranges are INCLUSIVE; iterate 0..len-1 and guard empties.

<a id="sym-block_root"></a>
### `block_root` · fn

```
block_root(records<Vec<Record>>)<String> ->
```

Block digest over an ordered set of records: the Merkle–Damgård fold
sha256( sha256("") ++ d(r0) ++ d(r1) ++ ... ), where d(r) is the per-record
digest. It is content- AND order-dependent — any change to a record, its
position, or the count changes the result — so it legitimizes an ordered
fact set. Empty -> sha256("").
(A full Merkle tree was tried here; this toolchain build asserts in LLVM
codegen on the nested Vec<Vec<..>> fold, so the sequential fold is used —
it is strictly stronger for this purpose: order is binding, which a tree
would not be.)

**Relationships**

- calls [`record_digest`](#sym-record_digest)
- calls [`sha256`](crypto.md#sym-sha256)
- uses type [`Record`](#sym-record)

### `deserialize` · fn

```
deserialize(text<String>)<Chain> ->
```

Parse `text` (the output of `serialize`) back into a Chain. Field splits use
the TAB character, so values may contain any other byte. Malformed input
yields a 0-block chain (callers gate on `verify`, which is false for a
chain whose blocks don't line up with the text they came from).

<a id="sym-serialize"></a>
### `serialize` · fn

```
serialize(chain<Chain>)<String> ->
```

Machine serialization (tab- and newline-delimited). Layout:
  O<TAB>origin
  B<TAB>index<TAB>prev<TAB>root<TAB>hash          (per block, then its records)
  R<TAB>label<TAB>value                           (per record)
A label must never contain a tab (values may contain tabs -> label is the
first field, everything after the second tab is the value). This is the form
a consumer PERSISTS (VybOS index.json, a VybForge manifest sidecar, a
smuggle receipt); `deserialize` + `verify` re-establish integrity after any
on-disk tamper.

**Relationships**

- mentions [`deserialize`](#sym-deserialize)
- mentions [`verify`](#sym-verify)
- uses type [`Chain`](#sym-chain)

<a id="sym-signed_append"></a>
### `signed_append` · fn

```
signed_append(sc<SignedChain>, records<Vec<Record>>, seed<String>, old_seed<String>)<SignedChain> ->
```

Append a block sealing `records`, signed by `seed`. If the new block's signer
differs from the previous (key rotation), the PREVIOUS key (`old_seed`) must
authorize the handoff via a `"rotate:"+new_signer` signature stored in
rotations[]; signed_verify enforces it. Value semantics: the caller's
SignedChain is untouched.

<a id="sym-signed_verify"></a>
### `signed_verify` · fn

```
signed_verify(sc<SignedChain>, registry_pub<String>)<Bool> ->
```

Full signature verification: block integrity (plain verify) AND each block's
Ed25519 signature under its recorded signer, AND trust-root anchoring (genesis
signer == registry_pub), AND each key rotation authorized by the old key.
Any tamper with a record/order/link/signer/signature/rotation -> false.

**Relationships**

- calls [`verify`](#sym-verify)
- calls [`ed25519_verify`](crypto.md#sym-ed25519_verify)
- uses type [`SignedChain`](#sym-signedchain)
